overview.title: Opus132
overview.summary: Opus132 belongs to the Early Romantic era — music by Ludwig van Beethoven.
overview.history: Opus132 is ready to explore on Lune. It is associated with Ludwig van Beethoven. Stylistically it sits in the Early Romantic world. Start by listening, then ask about the bars that surprise your hands. Place every phrase in the Early Romantic sound-world: how would someone from that time shape it?
highlights: Place every phrase in the Early Romantic sound-world: how would someone from that time shape it?

eraInfo.label: Early Romantic
eraInfo.story: Personal feeling steps forward. Rubato, dramatic contrasts, and singing melodies on the piano become part of the language.
tips: Balance heart with a steady left hand.

composerInfo.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
composerInfo.hook: Beethoven stretched classical clarity into stormy personal drama.

eraInfo.story: Emotion, colour, and storytelling. Expect sweeping lines, rich harmony, and moments that feel like scenes from a novel.

composerInfo.name: Frédéric Chopin
composerInfo.hook: Chopin wrote the piano’s private poetry — rubato, colour, and singing lines.
composerInfo.bio: Mazurkas dance with a lifted beat; preludes are mood rooms; melodies should speak like a voice. Keep the left hand calm support while the right hand sings.
composerInfo.full: Frédéric Chopin (1810–1849) was a Polish pianist-composer who made the piano sound intimate. Mazurkas dance with a lifted beat; preludes are mood rooms; melodies should speak like a voice. Keep the left hand calm support while the right hand sings.

composerInfo.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
composerInfo.hook: Beethoven stretched classical clarity into stormy personal drama.
composerInfo.bio: His middle and late works push rhythm, harmony, and form while staying deeply human — even as he lost his hearing. When you practise Beethoven, listen for bold contrasts: sudden softs, fierce accents, and long arcs that feel like a story.
composerInfo.full: Ludwig van Beethoven (1770–1827) began as a dazzling pianist in Vienna and became one of the most influential composers in Western music. His middle and late works push rhythm, harmony, and form while staying deeply human — even as he lost his hearing. When you practise Beethoven, listen for bold contrasts: sudden softs, fierce accents, and long arcs that feel like a story.

Late works were written through enormous personal struggle — listen for bold contrasts.

composerInfo.name: Ludwig van Beethoven

When you practise Beethoven, listen for bold contrasts: sudden softs, fierce accents, and long arcs that feel like a story.

chapters.title: The story of the piece
chapters.body: Chorale no. 1 is ready to explore on Lune. It is associated with Johann Sebastian Bach. Stylistically it sits in the Baroque world. Start by listening, then ask about the bars that surprise your hands. Place every phrase in the Baroque sound-world: how would someone from that time shape it?

chapters.title: Era · Baroque
chapters.body: Ornament, drive, and clear bass lines. Think dance rhythms, terraced dynamics (sudden soft/loud), and melodies that keep spinning forward.

chapters.title: About Johann Sebastian Bach
chapters.body: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) shaped Baroque counterpoint into music that still trains every serious pianist. Listen for independent voices, steady pulse, and ornaments that sparkle without rushing. In preludes, let patterns bloom; in chorales, hear every voice.
chapters.hook: Bach builds beauty from clear lines that weave together.
highlights: Bach is closely tied to the piano — tone and touch are part of the story.

composerInfo.bio: Listen for independent voices, steady pulse, and ornaments that sparkle without rushing. In preludes, let patterns bloom; in chorales, hear every voice.
composerInfo.full: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) shaped Baroque counterpoint into music that still trains every serious pianist. Listen for independent voices, steady pulse, and ornaments that sparkle without rushing. In preludes, let patterns bloom; in chorales, hear every voice.
highlights: Bach is closely tied to the piano — tone and touch are part of the story.

eraInfo.label: Baroque
eraInfo.story: Ornament, drive, and clear bass lines. Think dance rhythms, terraced dynamics (sudden soft/loud), and melodies that keep spinning forward.

composerInfo.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
composerInfo.hook: Bach builds beauty from clear lines that weave together.
composerInfo.bio: Listen for independent voices, steady pulse, and ornaments that sparkle without rushing. In preludes, let patterns bloom; in chorales, hear every voice.
composerInfo.full: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) shaped Baroque counterpoint into music that still trains every serious pianist. Listen for independent voices, steady pulse, and ornaments that sparkle without rushing. In preludes, let patterns bloom; in chorales, hear every voice.
highlights: Bach is closely tied to the piano — tone and touch are part of the story.

chapters.hook: Bach builds beauty from clear lines that weave together.
highlights: Bach is closely tied to the piano — tone and touch are part of the story.

chapters.body: Chorale no. 1 is ready to explore on Lune. It is associated with Johann Sebastian Bach. Stylistically it sits in the Baroque world. Start by listening, then ask about the bars that surprise your hands. Place every phrase in the Baroque sound-world: how would someone from that time shape it?

chapters.title: Era · Baroque
chapters.body: Ornament, drive, and clear bass lines. Think dance rhythms, terraced dynamics (sudden soft/loud), and melodies that keep spinning forward.

chapters.title: About Johann Sebastian Bach
chapters.body: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) shaped Baroque counterpoint into music that still trains every serious pianist. Listen for independent voices, steady pulse, and ornaments that sparkle without rushing. In preludes, let patterns bloom; in chorales, hear every voice.
chapters.hook: Bach builds beauty from clear lines that weave together.
highlights: Bach is closely tied to the piano — tone and touch are part of the story.

eraInfo.label: Baroque
eraInfo.story: Ornament, drive, and clear bass lines. Think dance rhythms, terraced dynamics (sudden soft/loud), and melodies that keep spinning forward.

composerInfo.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
composerInfo.hook: Bach builds beauty from clear lines that weave together.
composerInfo.bio: Listen for independent voices, steady pulse, and ornaments that sparkle without rushing. In preludes, let patterns bloom; in chorales, hear every voice.
composerInfo.full: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750) shaped Baroque counterpoint into music that still trains every serious pianist. Listen for independent voices, steady pulse, and ornaments that sparkle without rushing. In preludes, let patterns bloom; in chorales, hear every voice.
highlights: Bach is closely tied to the piano — tone and touch are part of the story.
